newsitem.title: UK: GUS says home shopping still difficult.
newsitem.headline: GUS says home shopping still difficult.

text.p: British home shopping group Great Universal Stores Plc on Thursday reported a dip in first half profits and said it was still facing difficult trading conditions in is mail order business.

Pretax profits fell to 235.6 million pounds ($389.2 million) from 237.5 million in the six months to September 30 1996. Sales rose to 1.21 billion pounds from 1.20 billion. The group offered a dividend of 5.5 pence, up from 5.0 pence a year ago.

The group, best known as the maker of the Burberry raincoat, had already flagged the profit downturn in October, when it said profits would be around one percent lower due to a fall in demand in home shopping.

"Trade continues to be difficult in the home shopping division," chairman Lord Wolfson of Sunningdale said in a statement. He said if the pound remained strong until the end of the year, this would affect results from overseas subsidiaries, particularly South Africa and Holland.
"Trading performance for the second half is expected to follow the pattern of the first six months," he said.

UK home shopping saw sales fall 2.4 percent on the previous year in a very competitive market. Profit increases by other divisions did not fully compensate for mail order's profit decline, the company said.
Home Shopping made operating profits of 61.3 million stg in the half year, down from 72.4 million. Sales fell to 859.9 million stg from 870.3 million.
Burberrys and Scotch House classic knitwear stores increased profits to 24.4 million stg from 23.2 million on sales of 130.9 million up from 124.0 million.

GUS, the UK market leader in mail order, said it was improving warehousing and distribution systems for home shopping and the costs of these changes, which were charged to revenue, depressed trading profits.
GUS said Burberrys' results were affected by a decline in Japanese and South East Asian tourist trade in many of its international markets.
Royalty income was affected by the strength of sterling particularly against the yen and the group expected this to have an impact for the rest of the year.

The firm's CCN information services division boosted profits in the UK and overseas. GUS said its purchase in November of Experian, a leading U.S. supplier of credit, marketing and real estate information services, would immediately enhance earnings and generate strong cash flow.

The group said it received an 8.9 million stg credit for overpaid VAT and related interest in the first half. A credit of 9.7 million stg is expected in the second half, making 18.6 million in total, similar to last year's 18.8 million.
